deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page): X is a space with a closed stratum Y and open complement X* = X∖Y. V_{Y,X} is a (germ of a) tubular or regular neighbourhood of Y in X, and V*_{Y,X} = V_{Y,X} ∖ Y is the deleted neighbourhood. X is viewed as obtained by gluing V_{Y,X} and X* along V*_{Y,X}. The gluing is read as a pushout in spaces or topoi of the diagram X* ← V* → V.

This page states the homotopical version. Given a sufficiently flexible theory of homotopy types, the homotopy type of X should be the 'amalgamated sum' (homotopy pushout) of the homotopy types of three objects: X* and the two 'germs' ϑ*_{Y,X} and ϑ_{Y,X}. The latter two are 'infinitesimal', i.e. germs of neighbourhoods along Y, so in effect pro-homotopy types. ϑ*_{Y,X} is what is now called the (homotopy) link of Y in X.

Truncating to 1-types ('killing π_i for i≥2') gives a van Kampen theorem for fundamental groupoids. The square (8) is cocartesian in groupoids: π1(ϑ*_{Y,X}) maps by p to π1(ϑ_{Y,X}) ≅ π1(Y) and by i to π1(X*), and the dotted pushout is π1(X).

The next page specializes this to groups when everything is connected: π1X ≅ π1X* *_{π1V*} π1Y. The remaining task is to make π1(V*) explicit, which is the local datum (the link group). The purpose is a dévissage of the fundamental group(oid) and homotopy type of a stratified space (e.g. moduli stacks with the boundary divisor as Y) into elementary local and global pieces.
errors: Not an error but an implicit hypothesis: π1(ϑ_{Y,X}) ≅ π1(Y) needs V to deformation-retract onto Y (regular/tubular neighbourhood, conical structure, tame topology). Grothendieck flags on the previous page that he wants to proceed independently of normal local triviality, so this would have to be justified by a tameness condition.

The pushout is valid as a homotopy pushout, i.e. with groupoids on many base points (Brown's van Kampen). Naively passing to groups requires connectedness of V*, which the next page assumes. In codimension 1 V* can be disconnected and one gets HNN-type amalgams; the groupoid formulation chosen here handles this correctly.

ideas.what: Decomposition of a stratified space as the homotopy pushout of the complement, the neighbourhood germ of the stratum, and the punctured neighbourhood germ (link)
ideas.modern_name: homotopy pushout along the homotopy link; stratified dévissage
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quinn (homotopically stratified sets, 1988); Siebenmann; later Lurie, Woolf and others (exit paths, stratified homotopy theory)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (§5–6: tame topology, dévissage of stratified structures, tubular neighbourhoods); La Longue Marche (gluing and van Kampen for moduli)

ideas.what: Van Kampen theorem for fundamental groupoids applied to stratum, complement and link
ideas.usually_credited_to: R. Brown (1967); Grothendieck SGA1 Exposé IX (descent and van Kampen for étale π1)
ideas.where_published: SGA1 Exp. IX; Esquisse d'un programme

ideas.what: Neighbourhood germs and punctured neighbourhoods treated as 'infinitesimal' homotopy types
ideas.modern_name: pro-homotopy types of germs / tubular neighbourhood germs (cf. SGA2 local fundamental groups, Artin–Mazur)
ideas.where_published: SGA2 (local π1 of punctured neighbourhoods); Esquisse d'un programme

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard van Kampen and homotopy-pushout decomposition of a stratified space via complement, neighbourhood and link. It matches ideas already sketched in Esquisse d'un programme and developed later by Quinn, Brown, Lurie and others. Nothing new on this page.
transcription_corrections: The struck word above ϑ is 'types', replaced by the quoted insertion "germes". The reading 'des trois "germes"' is consistent with the image.
The symbols written ϑ*_{Y,X}, ϑ_{Y,X} on this page are Grothendieck's handwritten V*_{Y,X}, V_{Y,X} (the same objects as on the previous page), probably understood as germs.
